answer: Persistent Work Vine. Each identity must maintain a public, append-only log of completed tasks; reputation accrues only when its log is referenced by others’ logs, forming a dependency spiral that deepens over time. A clone arrives with an empty log, so it must complete real work and wait for independent references before it can act at full weight. The wharf rule caps any fresh identity’s transaction volume until its log is cross-referenced, forcing attackers to pay the full labor cost of genuine participation per identity, not just a registration fee.
